documents.title: Emergency Department Record (received)
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital emergency department. Arrival 6/4/2025 14:20 by ambulance; discharged 6/5/2025 16:00 from the ED observation unit. Record faxed 7/29/2025 after a second request.

CC: altered and sweaty after pesticide application.

HPI: 33-year-old male farm pest control worker. Crew found him confused and drenched in sweat in a field where he had been applying pesticide for several hours. Before he went down he told them his vision was blurry, he couldn't catch his breath and his stomach was cramping. They pulled him away from the treated rows and called EMS.

PMH none. PSH tonsillectomy in childhood. Meds none. Allergies: NKDA. FH father DM2, mother HTN. SH never smoker, alcohol 1-2 drinks/month.

Triage VS: BP 92/56, HR 48, RR 28, SpO2 88% on RA.

Exam: disoriented, salivating heavily. Pupils pinpoint, still reactive. Tearing, nasal discharge. Fasciculations throughout. Expiratory wheeze, bronchospastic. Bradycardic. Bowel sounds hyperactive; large-volume watery stool. Skin cool, clammy, profuse sweat.

ED course: clothing removed and bagged, skin washed. Supplemental O2. Atropine IV in repeated doses until secretions dried and wheeze cleared. Pralidoxime IV. By 17:30 HR 92, BP 112/70, RR 18, SpO2 96% on 2 L; mentation clearing. RBC acetylcholinesterase 3100 U/L, low. BMP and CBC unremarkable. Held in observation overnight; no recurrent symptoms, weaned to room air.

Diagnosis: organophosphate poisoning, occupational exposure.

Disposition: home 6/5, VS at discharge BP 118/74, HR 78, RR 16, SpO2 98% RA. No prescriptions. No pesticide handling until cleared to return. Follow up with primary care in 1 week. Return for sweating, drooling, weakness or trouble breathing.

documents.title: ER Visit
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi doc, just letting you know I was in the ER last week. I got sick from the spray at work and they kept me overnight. I'm ok now and back on the crew since Monday. Paper says follow up with you, do I need to?

documents.title: RE: ER Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Ramon, glad you're feeling better. Yes, I would like to see you after an exposure like that, so I can go over what happened and talk about protecting yourself at work. Call the front desk or book on the portal for any open slot this week or next. In the meantime, if the sweating, drooling, weakness or breathing trouble come back, go straight to the ER. We're requesting the hospital's record.

documents.title: Records Request
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Faxed request to the regional hospital ED for 6/4 visit records, release on file. Will refax in 2 weeks if nothing received.

documents.title: Records Request, Second
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: No records yet from the hospital for 6/4. Called their HIM office, they had no request on file. Refaxed. Pt has not booked the follow-up visit.

documents.title: Annual Physical Due
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Hi Ramon, you're due for your yearly physical this month. Use the portal to pick a time or call us, and we can also go over your ER visit from June at the same appointment.

documents.title: Immunization Report: Retail Pharmacy
documents.author: pharmacy
documents.body: Immunization registry update. Influenza vaccine, trivalent, 0.5 mL IM, left deltoid, given 10/21/2025 at a retail pharmacy. No adverse reaction reported.

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary (received)
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital. Admitted 6/5/2026 via the ED to the medical ICU; transferred to the medical floor 6/8; discharged home 6/9/2026.

Admitting diagnosis: organophosphate insecticide poisoning, second occupational episode (prior ED treatment June 2025).

Presentation: 34-year-old man who was mixing a liquid insecticide bare-handed when coworkers noticed he was sweating heavily and drooling. Vomited several times en route and his breathing worsened. EMS found miosis and thick oral secretions that were hard to clear; they took off his contaminated shirt and flushed his skin with water.

Allergies: NKDA. Home meds: none.

Arrival: anxious, diaphoretic, air hungry, with secretions audible across the room. Cool clammy skin, lacrimation, rhinorrhea. Diffuse wheeze with crackles bilaterally. Visible fasciculations of both forearms and calves. Following commands, speaking only a few words at a time. No signs of trauma. HR 44 with a thready pulse, BP 98/60, RR 30, SpO2 87% on non-rebreather. Fingerstick glucose 94.

Hospital course: airway suctioned aggressively and intubation equipment readied. Atropine boluses escalated, then a continuous infusion; secretions dried and oxygenation improved, so he was never intubated. Pralidoxime infusion. Decontamination completed in the ED. By the next morning HR 96, BP 118/72, SpO2 95% on 2 L nasal cannula. Atropine weaned off over 48 hours without recurrence; pralidoxime stopped. Moved to the floor 6/8, on room air, eating and walking. No complications.

Labs: RBC acetylcholinesterase 2400 U/L on admission (low), 2900 U/L on 6/9. BMP and CBC within normal limits.

Discharge diagnosis: organophosphate poisoning, accidental, recurrent occupational exposure.
Discharge vitals: HR 76, BP 120/76, RR 16, SpO2 98% RA.
Discharge medications: none.

Instructions: no mixing or applying pesticides until cleared to return. Gloves and full protective gear for any future chemical handling. See PCP after discharge. Return for sweating, drooling, muscle twitching, weakness or shortness of breath.

documents.title: Hospital
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, I was in the hospital again from the bug spray, in the ICU for a few days this time. I've been home since last Tuesday. They told me to see you. I'm not working right now.

documents.title: RE: Hospital
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Ramon, I'm sorry, that sounds frightening. Please come in soon, ideally within the next week or two. This is the second time and I want to go through it with you in person. The front desk will reach out with times. If any of the symptoms come back, call 911. We'll ask the hospital to send their records.

documents.title: Records Request
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Faxed records request to the regional hospital for admission 6/5-6/9/2026. Left pt a message with two open appointment times next week; asked him to call back.

documents.title: Outreach Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Hospital discharge summary came in 7/21; PCP asked that we get him in. Called his cell, no answer, left a voicemail asking him to call to book a visit. Portal message also sent. Not scheduled at this time.
